full_judgment: 4. Defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable as framed. The suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It is barred by limitation. It is bad for defect of parties. The further case of this defendant is that Chuni Lal Sen and others, the original owners of the suit properties, left for India in 1950 without disposing of the suit properties as a result of which there was none to pay the rent of the same. As such, the suit properties were sold in auction on account of non-payment of rent. In auction, the suit properties were sold to defendant No. 1 on 30.10.1963 and sale was duly confirmed on 30.12.1963. Accordingly, the suit properties became the khash land of khatian No. 1 of the government. Subsequently, suit plot Nos. 1109, 1115, 1111 were leased out to different persons in Settlement Case No. 142 BH/63-64 and those lessees had been possessing the same. Masuma Khatoon Girls' High School has been running in suit plot No. 1102 contiguous to suit plot No. 1103. This defendant got settlement of the entire land of suit plot No.1103 in two instalments. Defendant No. 3 constructed a semi pucca but on the leased land and had since been in possession thereof. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 358 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif for permanent injunction in respect of the suit properties but the suit was dismissed on 11.8.1984. There are one temple and a building in the suit plot No. 1103 and Nanibala Datta had been living in that building as a licensee under the original owner. When she left the building during the War of Liberation in 1971, the plaintiff illegally entered into the building by breaking open the lock and continued his illegal possession in the building of suit plot No.1103. To legalise his unlawful possession, the plaintiff collusively created an antedated agreement claiming the suit properties by forging the signature of deceased Birendra Nath Sen Gupta who left the country for India before 15.5.67 and died there. On 28.6.1982, the plaintiff was evicted from his unlawful possession of the suit properties. The plaintiff filed a petition for getting lease of the suit properties before the appropriate authority on different occasions admitting the suit properties to be the khas land of the government. Title Appeal No. 15 of 1979 preferred by the government was allowed on contest setting aside the decree passed in favour of the plain-tiff in Title Suit No. 54 of 1968. Subsequently, the defendant was given lease of the entire land of suit plot No. 1103 permanently. For the reasons stated, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with costs.
